clue.text: Bad tweet bothers chap leaving Conservative authority

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt or in poor order, so the letters need rearranging
one thing leaving another means it goes away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An offensive social-media post upsets a man who has quit the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP loses its C to leave HAP, which joins TWEET BOTHERS in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The powers that be is an idiom for those in control, the people holding official power over others.

clue.text: Resin from tree put in ground with nitrogen

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A recipe for extracting resin from a tree, ground up with a nitrogen fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nitrogen' adds an N to the letters of TREE PUT IN before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is the oleoresin tapped from pine trees, so it is a resin in the broad sense.

clue.text: Prodigal, more disheartened tramp

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: extra means more, additional
a vagrant is a tramp

explanation.surface: A wastrel who is more downcast than any vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: VAGRANT has seven letters; removing its central R leaves VAGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal, as in the prodigal son, means recklessly wasteful with money, the same as extravagant.

clue.text: Submissive old criminal holding spotted cube

parts.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or criminal
a die is a cube marked with spots

explanation.surface: A meek former crook clutching a dice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted cube' sounds like something seen, but a cube marked with spots is a dice; 'criminal' is British slang, as in a corrupt copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone submissive yields to authority, which is what being obedient means: doing as one is told.

clue.text: Better prospect initially missed in conclusion

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: the end is the conclusion

indicators.note: the opening letter is the one that goes missing from the word

parts.note: a chance is a prospect, a likelihood

explanation.surface: A prospect overlooked at first improved the ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective or adverb, but it is a past participle meaning improved.
explanation.definitionFit: Better here is a past participle adjective, as in improved; enhanced likewise means made better.

clue.text: Pacific state importing South Indian pastry

indicators.note: a country importing goods brings them inside its borders

parts.note: Samoa is an island nation in the Pacific
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: An island nation bringing in goods from southern India.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry with a savoury filling, from Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Skinful had on Burns Night?

parts.note: surface reading: a skinful of drink downed on the night honouring the poet Robert Burns
setter's reading: a dish that is literally a skin filled with stuffing, the centrepiece of the Burns supper

explanation.walkthrough: A skinful is British slang for a lot of alcohol; Burns Night (25 January) is the Scottish celebration of the poet with whisky and a traditional supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is minced offal and oatmeal cooked in a sheep's stomach, so it is a skin full, eaten on Burns Night.

clue.text: Slow boat nevertheless capsized

indicators.note: a boat that has capsized is upside down, which in a down entry turns the word end to end

parts.note: but means nevertheless, however

explanation.surface: A sluggish vessel that turned over regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a slang term for a clumsy, slow-moving old boat.

clue.text: Energy worker climbing fiery mountain

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down entry that means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a worker ant; ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An energetic labourer scaling a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna in Sicily is an active volcano, hence a mountain that spits fire.

clue.text: Rook: different meat in northern town

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
other means different
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A shopping list of a bird and an unusual meat, found up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotherham is a town in South Yorkshire, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotherham is an industrial town in Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Chat referring to African country

parts.note: to gab is to chat
on means about, referring to

explanation.surface: Small talk about a country in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the west coast of central Africa.

clue.text: Number one story recalled euphoria

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Remembering a chart-topping tale brought great joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a single unit meaning a hit, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation and euphoria are synonyms for an intense feeling of happiness.

clue.text: Fools backing postgraduate in disgrace

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool
MA, Master of Arts, is a postgraduate degree

explanation.surface: Idiots who support a graduate student fall into disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: Black dog barking in hall came to catch ball

indicators.note: catching something means taking hold of it, so one letter ends up inside the rest
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A dog barking in the hallway came to fetch a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Black dog is Churchill's famous name for his depression, so the dog is not a pet at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholia is deep depression, which Winston Churchill called his black dog.

clue.text: Two poor grades produce decline

parts.note: D and E are two low exam grades
to generate is to produce

explanation.surface: A student's two bad marks lead to a downward slide.
explanation.definitionFit: To degenerate is to decline or deteriorate in quality.

clue.text: Railway Children amuse themselves with school group

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
a set is a group

explanation.surface: It looks like a remark about the characters of the novel The Railway Children at play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Railway Children is E. Nesbit's classic novel, but read literally it means children who play at railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy model railway, which children play with.

clue.text: Down and dirty

definitions.meaning: second meaning: smutty, indecent, as in a risqué joke or film

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down and dirty' reads as one phrase meaning gritty, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means both melancholy in mood and sexually explicit, as in blue movies.

clue.text: Marine ray devouring river fish

parts.note: marine means of the sea

indicators.note: something devoured is swallowed and ends up inside the eater

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sea creature, a ray, eating a fish from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' wants to be the fish here; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bream is a family of edible marine fish.

clue.text: On the warpath in uniform, spike the guns?

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to spike is to pin, pierce with a point
arms are weapons such as guns

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform ready for battle, spiking the enemy's guns.
explanation.walkthrough: To spike a gun was to disable it by driving a spike into its touch-hole; here it simply pairs a pin with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for angry and ready to fight, which is what being on the warpath means.

clue.text: Northern origins in Open All Hours for Arkwright?

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Northern
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A question about Arkwright, the shopkeeper in the British sitcom Open All Hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Open All Hours was a BBC sitcom set in a northern corner shop run by Arkwright; read as ark-wright, an ark builder, the name points to the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is a builder, and the Bible's famous ark builder was the patriarch who survived the Flood.

clue.text: Son and peers devised reply

indicators.note: devised means invented or put together, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: son and peers taken as written, the and only joining them

explanation.surface: A boy and his fellows came up with an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, an answer given to something said.

clue.text: How's that for charm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, 'How's that?' (Howzat) is the fielders' call asking the umpire for a dismissal

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout 'How's that?' to the umpire when they think a batsman is out; that shout is an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketers' cry is formally an appeal to the umpire, and appeal also means attractiveness or charm.

clue.text: Bar one, wise men understood larval form

indicators.note: bar means except, so the word is taken without the letter standing for one

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: Apart from one, the sages grasped the grub's form.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGI loses I, the Roman one, leaving MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the larva of a fly, so it is a larval form.

clue.text: More work in uncut opiate

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: More of the drug in its unadulterated state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book, not the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the famous book written by Sir Thomas More describing an ideal island society.

clue.text: Wailing wraith, that woman in torment

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a bane is a source of torment
she refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A shrieking ghost, a woman in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose wailing foretells a death.

clue.text: Bit of leg that's a little lower?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg
second meaning: a lower is something that lows (moos), and a little one is a young cow

explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'further down', fitting the leg, but it is low-er, a mooing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the shin shares its name with a young bovine, a small mooer.

clue.text: Floor in a labyrinth

parts.note: taken as written
a maze is a labyrinth

explanation.surface: A floor laid out inside a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to stun.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to astonish them completely, the same as to amaze.

clue.text: Excellent reason to start with melody

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: to start points at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of reason

explanation.surface: A first-rate excuse to begin with a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, as in Air on the G String.

clue.text: Irregular mostly involved with Left?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier usually linked with left-wing causes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: irregulars fighting outside regular armies, many in left-wing insurgencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter, and many famous guerrilla movements, like Che Guevara's, were left-wing.

clue.text: Toast of lord made silly by rice wine?

indicators.note: being made silly means turned foolish and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
by means multiplied by, as in three by four
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A nobleman's toast goes giggly after too much rice wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but means times, as in multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: For old times' sake is a phrase raised as a toast in memory of shared past days.
